classification.difficultyReason: Infer a base angle from tangent perpendicularity, transfer it through the equal radii to find the central angle, and use the alternate segment theorem for z.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: Circle with centre O, horizontal tangent PQ at the bottom vertex, an inscribed triangle, and dashed radii to the bottom and right-hand vertices. Ordinary source colours become black. Geometry is reconstructed consistently with the given tangent–chord angle.
spec.mathematics: The tangent–chord angle is 56°. x lies between the right-hand radius and the chord to the tangent point; y is the central angle subtending that chord; z is the corresponding circumference angle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 56° and unknown labels x, y and z appear. Supplied numerical answers are omitted.

answer.worked:
The radius is perpendicular to the tangent. The two radii form an isosceles triangle, so its base angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}x&=90^\circ-56^\circ\\x&=34^\circ\\y&=180^\circ-2\times34^\circ\\y&=112^\circ\end{align*}$$
By the alternate segment theorem,
$$z=56^\circ.$$
